answer: Each identity posts a 200-unit bond sealed by a hardware kernel credential and a registration cipher unique to that device. Minting N fakes locks 200×N units, slashes 100 percent of every proven duplicate bond, and waits 20 epochs before release. Splitting identities gains nothing because marginal cost stays 200 per fake, shared penalties hit the bond pool, and independent jurors flag duplicates under the velvet audit.
